sentences.text:
The President Harun Mahamudkha Pathan vs The Education
Officer (Primary) Zilha ... on 4 March, 2019

Author: M. S. Karnik
Bench: S. C. Dharmadhikari, M. S. Karnik
 (19) wp-5083-
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Writ Petition No.5083 Of 2018
 The President, Harun Mahamudkha Pathan .. Petitioner
 Vs
 The Education Officer (Primary), Zilla
 Parishad, Solapur and Ors. .. Respondents
 Mr.Ashok B. Tajane for the Petitioner.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Mr.Anand S. Kulkarni for Respondent
 No.1.

Mr.S.B.Kalel, Agp for State-Respondent
 Nos.3 and 4.
 Coram :- S. C. Dharmadhikari &
 M. S. Karnik, Jj.
 Date :- March 4, 2019
 P.C. :-
1.
After our earlier order, which was fairly detailed, passed on 4th February, 2019, now an inspection has been carried out.
This inspection report shows that the petitioner's school lacks in basic amenities.
For instance, the toilet blocks, separately for children (girl child and male child), are not in the required numbers.
Further, the inspection report reveals that the school management does not understand the basic difference between the facilities or amenities like a changing room, a toilet and a urinal.

The ordinary dictionary meaning of these terms is as under :-
M.M.Salgaonkar (19) wp-5083-18.doc Lavatory - A large receptacle for urine + faeces usually with running water and a flush mechanism as a means of disposal.
Toilet - Lavatory  Urinal - a sanitary fitting usually against a wall,
for men to urinate into.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As far as the male students are concerned, the facility of a urinal not enclosed from all sides, may serve their purpose, but that cannot be equated with toilets.
As far as the girl child is concerned, she requires an adjacent room or other space separated from the toilet block and for them a urinal will never suffice.
This difference can be outlined by referring to the settled sanitation standards.

3. We gave, for instance, an illustration that when there are sports activities in a primary school and required under the law to be compulsorily carried out, they may be during school hours or thereafter, but surely for a child to get into the sportswear,
a girl child specially, will require the privacy of a changing room.
She can then change the clothes without any inhibition.
In the school compound and in open, this is impossible.
Secondly, it is also not possible in the presence of other girls to get into such gear in a toilet block.
The toilet blocks surely cannot be utilized for such purpose.
M.M.Salgaonkar (19) wp-5083-18.doc 4.

When the requirement is that all the children shall be provided with hygienic and clean food cooked within the premises, then, having a kitchen far away and that too, a fiber shed, but not in use in this case, would be a very serious lapse or deficiency.

The food, which has to be compulsorily provided in the school for the children's nutrition and nourishment, is procured, in this case, from outside, but nobody has deposed on oath that the food item meets the standards and norms prescribed by law and at least by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
Ultimately the food is administered to and consumed by the children.
It should not only be cooked in a hygienic set up, but it has to be served on every working day during intervals and recess.

There could be short recesses and the requirement of food would depend upon whether it is served at the time of breakfast or lunch.
5.
In such circumstances, we expected that somebody would go and regularly inspect the facility where this food is cooked.

It may be cooked in their kitchen by women self-help groups, however,
whether it can be consumed or it is fit for eating after it is transported from the premises of these women self-help groups to the school, has not been stated at all.
M.M.Salgaonkar (19) wp-5083-18.doc 6.

Unfortunately, the Deputy Director of Education, Pune Region, Pune, who is present in Court and who is deponent of this affidavit on behalf of the State and the Department, is unable to throw light and beyond stating that the basic amenities and facilities are lacking, she could not even apprise us of the required standards and norms.
The standards and norms are set out either in the rules or regulations or guidelines issued from time to time, so as to fulfill the object and purpose of the Right to Education Act, 2009.
The Act has been enacted in the year 2009 and we have yet to see its full compliance.
The Act is now a decade old.
Once we have achieved this much, namely, making an enactment, we must be aware that people are not satisfied with mere making of the law, but its effective implementation.

sentences.text: 2 7. Mr.Tajane now accepts that there are deficiencies and in terms of the State's affidavit, but prays that time be granted to the petitioner to provide the basic amenities and remove all deficiencies.
8. We are least impressed by his submission for the simple reason that the report indicates that though the school building has some rooms and 18 in number, there is only one ramp.
That also has not been provided in terms of the standards and norms prescribed in law.
The school playground does not have a M.M.Salgaonkar (19) wp-5083-18.doc compound wall.
Further, the school has procured the playground facility on payment of rent.
Surely, the premises or land is belonging to somebody else, but that is used by the school as a playground.
The school must invest its own funds in construction of a playground and for the construction of a compound wall surrounding the entire playground.
It should have entry and exit gates and manned by security guards.

In recent times,
ghastly crimes are committed and school going children are the unfortunate victims.
Thus, the school going children are victims of heinous crimes and perversity in the society.
If the area, where they play, is unsecured and unprotected, then, it is only a waiting game.
We are waiting for disasters and crimes to happen.
9. As is the state of the kitchen shed, ditto is the condition of the library.
The library does not have any record of the books collected, distributed and returned.
Apart from these facilities which are hopelessly lacking, we have found another serious deficiency in that, there is no toilet facility for the disabled children.
In fact, the report says that there is no provision for such facility for the disabled.
It is time we realise that special minor children have equal rights and on par with the abled.
They are meritorious and equally deserve a opportunity to take primary education.

Those administering and managing educational institutions ought to realise that quality teaching M.M.Salgaonkar (19)
wp-5083-18.doc includes catering to the need of differently abled.
Therefore, a toilet for the disabled is the need of the hour.
Similar is the case about lack of drinking water.
That is not only to be provided, but it must be ensured that it is clean.
10. What we have before us in the form of numbers, the student strength.
There are 716 students in the school and there are 20 teachers.

Now the proportion or the student teacher ratio may be proper, but we find that when the basic amenities and facilities are to be mandatorily provided,
then, unless a corpus is built, and there is a continuous flow of funds, these provisions and their maintenance will be impossible.
The petitioner cannot depend only upon the non-salary grant received from the Government.

11. In the above circumstances, we direct the petitioner Sanstha to show its bona fides and before granting it time to put all things in place, a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- should be deposited by it in this Court and within a period of two weeks from today.
After that sum is deposited, the petitioner has to state on affidavit, a time-schedule within which all the basic mandatory facilities, amenities which are hopelessly lacking, would be provided.
We would not hesitate to pass an order refusing permission to the petitioner to admit any student for the Academic Year 2019-2010 in first standard or Pre-K.G.
Let the needful be done.
M.M.Salgaonkar (19) wp-5083-18.doc 12.
Equally, we remind all the authorities and particularly, those In-charge of primary education that the illustration of this institution should be enough for them to start an inspection all around.

sentences.text: 3 They must regularly inspect the primary schools within their jurisdiction and ensure that all safety and security measures, basic amenities are in place.
If not, proper fines be imposed and for repeaters, they have to be in addition to other penalties.
If the officers are not attending duties and failing to carry out periodical inspection, let disciplinary action be taken against them.
If that is not taken, we would not hesitate to punish the Directors and Deputy Directors of Education and Education Officers as also the Chief Executive Officer of Zilla Parishads.
We would then direct that action be initiated against them by their superiors.

We would not hesitate to direct recovery measures against erring officials so that substantial amounts can be recovered from their salaries and perquisites and with that sum the deficiencies be removed.

There should be proper schemes to take over such schools and allow them to be run, managed and administered by other educational institutions or managements who have experience, expertise and equally do not have problem of funds.
There should be certain reputation acquired before permissions are granted to run or establish a school.
The bona fides of such people will have to be tested and with appropriate M.M.Salgaonkar (19) wp-5083-18.doc monetary deposits being insisted before approval or permission is granted.
These sums be then invested so that they earn interest and thereafter from the interest amount, basic amenities can be provided.
Everything requires funds and by imposition of fines or suitable measures, that can be generated.
We do not think that the legal infrastructure is lacking in any manner in this behalf.
13. We post this matter on 1st April, 2019 for passing further orders.

(M.S.KARNIK, J.) (S.C.DHARMADHIKARI, J.)
